cards: What is endotoxin chemically?
Lipopolysaccharide of the Gram-negative outer membrane
Which part of lipopolysaccharide is biologically active?
Lipid A
Which lipopolysaccharide part is unique to each organism?
The O antigen polysaccharide
What makes a lipopolysaccharide rough, semi-rough or smooth?
The number of repeating O antigen units
When is endotoxin released?
On cell lysis, including by antibiotics, and during rapid growth
Which receptor carries the innate response to lipopolysaccharide?
A Toll-like receptor, with a lipopolysaccharide binding complex
What do high endotoxin levels do to neutrophils?
Interfere with chemotaxis to the infection site
What is warm shock?
Early septic shock: vasodilation with cardiac output at first rising
Which three properties sort the Gram-negative bacilli?
Oxygen requirement, lactose fermentation and the oxidase enzyme
Which oxidase-positive pair stands apart from the enterics?
Haemophilus and Pasteurella
Which Gram-negative rod is the obligate anaerobe in the scheme?
Bacteroides
Which pair of nonenteric aerobes are zoonotic pathogens?
Brucella and Francisella
Which flagellum pattern do pseudomonads have?
A single polar flagellum
Which pigment and odor mark Pseudomonas aeruginosa?
Greenish-blue pyocyanin and a grapelike odor
Why does Pseudomonas aeruginosa contaminate ventilators and intravenous lines?
It produces biofilms
What does Pseudomonas exotoxin A inhibit?
Protein synthesis
What does Pseudomonas exoenzyme S induce?
Apoptosis of T cells
Which hosts get nosocomial Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection?
Patients with burns, neoplastic disease and cystic fibrosis
Which eye infection does Pseudomonas give contact lens wearers?
Corneal ulcers
Why might a Pseudomonas vaccine harm cystic fibrosis patients?
It may raise lung inflammation in chronic infection
Which Burkholderia is a copathogen in cystic fibrosis?
Burkholderia cepacia
Which disease does Burkholderia pseudomallei cause?
Melioidosis, from tropical soil and water
How long can Acinetobacter baumannii survive on fomites?
For months
Which Brucella species infect cattle and pigs?
Brucella abortus in cattle, Brucella suis in pigs
Why is brucellosis called undulant fever?
Its fever fluctuates over weeks to a year
Which laboratory test diagnoses brucellosis?
A serological agglutination titer test
What is tularemia's other name?
Rabbit fever
Why can tularemia relapse?
Francisella tularensis persists inside cells
Which cells does Bordetella pertussis bind and destroy?
Ciliated respiratory epithelial cells
Which pertussis stage brings the whoop?
The paroxysmal stage
Which pertussis stage resembles a cold?
The catarrhal stage
What kind of pertussis vaccine is DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis)?
Acellular: toxoid plus other antigens
Why are infants most at risk of pertussis?
Infants under 2 months cannot be vaccinated
Which medium grows Legionella?
Charcoal yeast extract agar
Which organisms does Legionella live with in water?
Amebas
How is Legionella transmitted?
By aerosols from water systems
Which oxygen pattern do all enterics share?
Facultative anaerobes
What do all enterics ferment?
Glucose
What separates coliforms from non-coliforms?
Coliforms ferment lactose
What do eosin methylene blue and MacConkey's agar select for?
Gram-negative bacteria
Which enteric antigen is flagellar?
The H antigen
Which enteric antigen is the capsule, Vi in Salmonella?
The K antigen
Which Escherichia coli strain causes traveler's diarrhea?
Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli
Which Escherichia coli strain causes a shigellosis-like disease?
Enteroinvasive Escherichia coli
Which Escherichia coli strain causes wasting infantile diarrhea?
Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli
Which Escherichia coli strain causes hemolytic uremic syndrome?
Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli O157:H7
What is the reservoir of Escherichia coli O157:H7?
The intestines of cattle
What color is Escherichia coli O157:H7 on Rainbow agar?
Black
What does the coliform count indicate in water?
Fecal contamination
Which coliform has a large capsule and causes nosocomial pneumonia?
Klebsiella pneumoniae
Which enteric makes the red pigment prodigiosin?
Serratia marcescens
Which enteric swarms across agar in waves?
Proteus vulgaris
Which stones is Proteus related to?
Bladder and kidney stones
Who are the only hosts of Salmonella typhi?
Humans
Where do chronic typhoid carriers shed the bacilli from?
The gallbladder
Which rash marks typhoid fever?
Rose-colored spots
Which Salmonella source is a pet reptile?
Pet turtles and bearded dragons
Which bowel does Shigella invade?
The large intestine
Does Shigella invade the blood?
No; it does not perforate or enter the blood
Which Yersinia infection can mimic appendicitis?
Yersinia enterocolitica, by inflaming the ileum
What staining pattern does Yersinia pestis show?
Bipolar staining
What blocks an infected flea's esophagus?
Clots made by the bacterium's coagulase
How does a blocked flea transmit plague?
It bites ravenously and regurgitates the bacteria
What is a bubo?
A swollen, necrotic lymph node in the groin or axilla
Which plague form is the black plague?
Septicemic plague, with purpura and gangrene
Which plague form spreads by aerosol?
Pneumonic plague
How is plague diagnosed?
History, symptoms and aspiration of the buboes
What is sylvatic plague?
Plague caught from wild animals
How do humans get Pasteurella multocida?
Animal bites or scratches
Why is Haemophilus grown on chocolate agar?
It needs hemin or nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide
Why is Haemophilus influenzae misnamed?
It does not cause the flu
What kind of vaccine is Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b)?
A subunit vaccine
Which Haemophilus species causes pink eye?
Haemophilus aegyptius
Which Haemophilus species causes chancroid?
Haemophilus ducreyi
Which Haemophilus species cause endocarditis after dental work?
Haemophilus parainfluenzae and Haemophilus aphrophilus
